title: Orchestrate staged build hooks and dependency sanitizer
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce staged prebuild pipeline and a dependency sanitizer that validates package manifest diffs and enforces curated upgrades. Backwards-compatible; toggled via repo feature flag.
description:
Motivation: Our CI has grown noisy and slow because full lint/test suites run for every push, and dependency bumps sometimes slip through without the intended curation. This PR introduces two coordinated improvements: (1) a staged build-hook orchestrator that runs quick sanity and path-aware linters first, then expanded checks only for affected packages; and (2) a dependency sanitizer that performs deterministic validation of package.json / lockfile diffs and rejects unsafe upgrades unless they match entries in the dep-curation manifest.

What this changes (single flow):
- Add .github/workflows/staged-ci.yml: a unified staged CI workflow with small, fast early lanes (quick-sanity, changed-path linting) and gated lanes (package lint, unit tests, integration smoke). Each lane is annotated with human-readable stage names and stage_timeout.
- Add tools/commit-paths.ts: utility to compute the set of repo packages and ownership paths touched by the diff; used to limit lint/test scope.
- Add scripts/dep_sanitizer.py: checks package manifest diffs, verifies lockfile integrity, and enforces dep-curation rules (allowed ranges and pinned-safe-flags). Emits machine-readable JSON for the bot to consume.
- Add build/hooks/README.md and small entrypoints for local dev (scripts/run-staged-ci.sh).
- Small changes to .github/labels.yml and CI job templates to expose retry and debug toggles.

Why this is different from prior PRs: Instead of just pruning tests or trimming matrices, this implements commit-path awareness and a deterministic sanitizer that ties dependency upgrades to a curated manifest. It avoids global test-skipping heuristics and focuses on reproducible gating.

- [x] Add sanitizer unit tests to simulate lockfile tampering and allowed vs disallowed upgrades
- [x] Run end-to-end against CI in feature branch

review_comments: Ben Cho: Can we add a retry wrapper around the integration smoke stage? We saw flakiness on linux-x86 jobs. Request: add RETRY_COUNT (default 2) and an opt-out DEBUG flag.
Asha Patel: Added RETRY_COUNT to job templates and a DEBUG_CI env toggle. Also added small perf backoff in scripts/run-staged-ci.sh (exponential backoff up to 3 retries).

Lina Gomez: Dep sanitizer looks good; one nit - please tighten error messages to include the offending package path and the offending lockfile entry. Also request adding a regression unit test for yarn -> npm lock conversions.
Asha Patel: Tightened messages and added regression fixture for lockfile conversion scenario.
ci_summary: Initial run: failed (lint error in sdk/js due to new stricter rule) -> author fixed and pushed. Second run: pass across all lanes (quick-sanity, path-lint, package-lint, unit, integration-smoke). Coverage unchanged. Lint warnings reduced by 12. Build artifacts: none (workflow-only change).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash after 2 approvals and green CI. Merge method: squash and merge. Changelog: internal; feature gated behind REPO_FEATURE_STAGED_CI.
testing_notes: Local: run scripts/run-staged-ci.sh --local to emulate staged lanes
Unit tests: commit-paths spec covers nested packages and symlinked paths
Sanitizer tests: fixture suite simulates allowed and disallowed upgrades, lockfile tampering
rollout_plan: Feature gated by REPO_FEATURE_STAGED_CI (default: off). We'll enable for a subset of CI runners (fastlane tag) for 48h, monitor failure rate in canary, then enable full-run. If dep_sanitizer rejects a PR, maintainers can re-run with bypass token after manual review.
notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing default test coverage. It is an orchestration and enforcement layer. If we see false-positives from the sanitizer, expand the dep-curation manifest and open ENG-8702 to triage recurring false-positives.
